absent: Value of PIPEFS_MAGIC and full pseudo filesystem context and dentry operation details
Implementation of pipe spin lock and unlock and initialization of read and write wait queues
Behavior of pipe state allocators, stream open helper, and iterated read and write handlers for named and anonymous pipes
Behavior of poll, ioctl, release, async and splice write handlers referenced by pipe operation tables
Rounding algorithm for pipe sizes and default values and limits for maximum size and per user page counts
Semantics of mount propagation flags beyond numeric values and of the missing flag bit not shown in this range
Numeric values of access list tags, permission bits, mode bits and wire version and layouts of wire header and entry structures
Identifier, namespace and idmapping translation helpers and validity predicates for user and group identifiers
Inode list caching, retrieval and timestamp and version update helpers beyond forget operations
Concrete inode set list implementations and ownership and capability checks for chmod and store paths

findings.text: A globally visible operations table for named pipes supplies open, iterated read, iterated write, poll, control, release, async and splice write handling, sharing its open routine with anonymous pipes.
Two outwardly callable cache helpers allow discarding a single cached list selected by type and discarding both cached lists held by an inode.
Two globally visible attribute handler tables publish the access and default list names and share a listing predicate that reports presence only when the backing inode supports such lists.
Outwardly callable helpers for simple filesystems store a supplied list with mode reconciliation and timestamp refresh, and derive fresh inode lists from a parent directory at creation.
Outwardly callable conversion helpers reconcile a mode value with a supplied list and decode a wire format buffer into an in memory list.

Opening a pipe or FIFO enters through a common routine that distinguishes anonymous objects by comparing the inode operations pointer against the anonymous table, then attaches or reuses pinned pipe state and dispatches on requested direction.
Filesystem startup registers a type named for pipes, mounts an internal instance, unwinds registration on mount failure, and records control parameters when that subsystem is enabled.
Context creation for the pipe filesystem initializes a pseudo filesystem context with its magic identifier and links dedicated superblock and dentry operation tables.
A control handler for the maximum pipe size funnels user and kernel value transfer through a rounding conversion so stored limits always respect pipe sizing granularity.

Access control library entry points validate ordering and mapping, test equivalence to mode bits, build a minimal three entry list from a mode, derive child lists from a parent default, adjust a list for chmod, and translate between memory and wire forms.
Storing a list enters through a gate that checks filesystem support, directory requirements for defaults, ownership or privilege, and validity before delegating to the inode specific store operation.
An inode holds at most one pipe state object shared by all openers, with a file count tracking attachments and the open file description caching the same object for later input and output.
Monotonic open counters and current reader and writer tallies are maintained separately so waiters can detect arrival of a partner by observing counter change while presence tests use tallies.
A freshly allocated or duplicated list starts with a single reference and records its entry count, with duplication preserving content while resetting sharing state.

Cached list invalidation leaves a do not cache marker untouched, otherwise atomically exchanges the slot to a not cached marker and releases the prior value unless it was already a non reference placeholder.

A valid list orders owner, optional named users, owning group, optional named groups, optional mask and other entries, requires mask when named entries exist, restricts permission bits to read write execute, and requires mapped identifiers.

Equivalence testing derives owner group and other permission triples from corresponding entries, applies mask to the group triple when present, flags presence of named or mask entries as not representable by mode alone, and optionally rewrites only permission bits of a supplied mode.

Creation from a parent default intersects owner group and other permissions with creation mode bits, prefers mask for group handling when present, records whether the result needs a separate access list, and propagates the default only to directories.
Chmod handling rewrites owner group and other permissions from the new mode, directing group bits to mask when present and otherwise to owning group, without altering named entries.

Wire decoding requires a present header, minimum header length, expected version and consistent entry count, rejects empty lists as absent, and validates tags and identifier conversion for named entries.

Wire encoding sizes output from entry count, writes version once, converts tags and permissions to little endian, maps identifiers through namespace translation with an undefined marker for non named entries, and reports required length when no buffer is supplied or range error when supplied space is short in the mapped variant.
Inode lock guards inspection and installation of the shared pipe object, with a second check after allocation to collapse races and free any surplus.
A per pipe mutex serializes open direction handling, counter and tally updates, and blocking decisions, held across partner wakeups and released on all success and failure exits.
Waiting for a partner drops the pipe spin protection while sleeping and reacquires it after wakeup, looping until the observed counter differs or a signal is pending.
Partner arrival is announced by waking all sleepers on the read queue, while abort paths wake writers or readers respectively when their tally drops to zero to avoid stranded waiters.
Named and anonymous pipe operation tables share open, poll, control, release, async and splice handlers and differ only in their iterated read and write handlers.
Pipe filesystem superblock handling pairs a non reclaiming inode destroy routine with a simple filesystem statistics routine.
Pipe filesystem registration pairs a textual name with context setup and anonymous superblock teardown callbacks.
Pipe control table holds three entries for maximum size and hard and soft per user page limits, each binding storage, length, access mode and a handler, with a lower bound of one on the first.
In memory access list layout comprises a reference count, an entry count and a trailing variable length entry array holding tag, permission and optional identifier fields.
Attribute handler tables for access and default lists each bind a well known name with a shared listing predicate.
Open direction dispatch accepts read only, write only, or combined access and rejects any other combination as invalid.

Named pipe opens block for a counterpart unless anonymous, already paired, opened for both directions, or nonblocking, with read only nonblocking recording the current writer epoch to defer hangup reporting and write only nonblocking failing immediately when no reader exists.
Partner wait snapshots a generation counter, sleeps interruptibly, then reports restart if still unchanged after a signal and success once another opener advances the counter.
Validation traverses tags through owner, named user section, owning group, named group section, mask and other stages, rejecting repeats, misordering, unknown tags and unterminated sequences.

Creation starts empty, bypasses symlinks and non supporting parents with umask application, bypasses absent defaults, otherwise clones and masks the parent default, keeps an access list only when not mode equivalent, and retains a default only for directories.

Chmod handling clones the current access list, rewrites permissions in the clone, replaces the original on success while releasing the predecessor, and delegates persistence to the inode store operation.
A signal pending after sleep aborts partner wait with a restart indication and unwinds the previously incremented tally with a wakeup when the last waiter departs.
Concurrent first opens may allocate duplicate pipe state, requiring the loser to increment the winner tally and release its own allocation to avoid leaks or split state.
Allocation failures for pipe state or access lists propagate out of memory errors without installing partial state.
Invalid open mode combinations and unsupported chmod or store attempts on filesystems without list support are rejected with dedicated error indications.
Malformed in memory lists with bad permission bits, misordered tags, unmapped identifiers or missing group or mask anchors are rejected during validation, equivalence, masking and chmod preparation.

Malformed wire buffers with missing header, short length, version mismatch, inconsistent count, unknown tags or invalid identifiers are rejected, and undersized output areas are reported as range errors.
Storing a default list on a non directory is forbidden when a value is present but treated as success when clearing, and storing without ownership or privilege is denied.
Mount propagation control flags are defined as single bit values with expire one, slave two, copy unbindable four, make shared eight, private sixteen and copy mount namespace file sixty four.
Pipe control parameters are named pipe-max-size, pipe-user-pages-hard and pipe-user-pages-soft, each with access mode 0644.
The pipe filesystem registers under the name pipefs and its mount propagation header is guarded by a once defined macro.
An idmapped mount helper walks all entries and rewrites named user and group identifiers through mount mapping while leaving other tags untouched.

Simple store updates the inode mode from the access list when applicable, refreshes modification time, advances version when enabled, caches the supplied lists, and drops creation references after caching.
Chmod and create helpers treat missing filesystem support as success with no work, propagate mapping and memory failures, and delegate final persistence to the inode specific store.
